minutes.headline: Planning Board recommended both zoning articles, adding a restaurant carryout parking floor amendment to the parking article.
minutes.summary: The board held an early informal talk on a Highland Street subdivision waiver (members opposed), continued a Flat Hill Road ANR plan over frontage and wetland questions, and held the public hearing on the two-family lot size and off-street parking articles. After closing the hearing it voted to recommend both articles, with a floor amendment on restaurant carryout parking. Committee reports and director's items followed, including 925 Mass Ave and the Brooks House.

public_comment.topic: Resident said he would hold comments for the public hearing and offered to report on the TC Pacios building committee.
Resident asked whether comments and questions would be allowed during the warrant article hearing.
Resident (Dave Rogers, 82 Highland Street) questioned the parking changes, two-family parking, town-owned property, quarter-mile off-site parking and warehouse numbers.
Resident asked why the parking section was being rewritten and raised concerns about child care, office spaces and stormwater runoff.
Resident asked for an update on maintenance of the detention basin between the Brooks House and the library.
Parks Commission member announced Earth Day week cleanup projects around town.

votes.motion: Continue the ANR plan for 360 Flat Hill Road to the April 26 meeting.
Close the public hearing on the zoning articles.
Recommend favorably both articles (two-family definition and off-street parking), with a floor amendment on article 29 adding one space per three seats for restaurant carryout.
Approve both sets of minutes from the March 22nd meeting.

budget_items.what_was_said: A possible brownfields cleanup grant was mentioned, with doubt that it would be enough for the contaminants found.
The director received a quote from MRPC for two master plan chapters. Capital planning provided funding and some has gone to the population study.
Capital planning voted to recommend raising the capital acquisition threshold, which goes to the finance committee.
A dollar figure for the rebuild article was expected before the next committee meeting. The proposal had come down from the original number.
Assessment work funding came through grants via MRPC, not town money.
A member noted parking space counts were part of cost-cutting discussions on the building.

decisions.decision: Applicant's attorney said they would likely not pursue the 319 Highland Street subdivision if the board opposed the frontage waiver; board members voiced opposition.
Board agreed in principle to develop a process so that a swapped plan resets the ANR clock.
Chair to reach out to the applicant's representative to attend the next meeting.
Director will email the MRPC master plan quote to the board for the next packet.
Board will hold a half-hour meeting at 8:30 before Town Meeting on May 1.
Director will reach out to the DPW director on the Brooks House detention basin maintenance and put an update on a future agenda.

what_happened.line: The Planning Board voted 4-0 to recommend both zoning articles, the two-family dwelling definition and off-street parking, with a floor amendment on restaurant carryout parking.
The board closed the public hearing on the zoning articles 4-0 after residents questioned the parking changes, including child care, stormwater runoff and off-site parking.
Board members voiced opposition to a frontage waiver for a Highland Street subdivision; the applicant's attorney said they would likely not pursue it if the board opposed.
The board continued the Flat Hill Road ANR plan to April 26 and agreed in principle to develop a process so a swapped plan resets the ANR clock.
The director will email the MRPC master plan quote for the next packet and follow up with DPW on the Brooks House detention basin.

why_it_matters: The two zoning articles, on two-family lots and off-street parking, now go to Town Meeting with the Planning Board's recommendation, so residents will be asked to vote on them and on the carryout parking requirement for restaurants.
The master plan quote and the ANR clock process show how the board plans to guide future development and how fast subdivision-type plans must be acted on.
watch_next: April 26 Planning Board meeting, when the Flat Hill Road ANR plan returns.
A half-hour Planning Board meeting at 8:30 before Town Meeting on May 1.
